advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test seeding $STATE_DIR/mcp-deployed-sha (and bot-deployed-sha) with a garbage/non-commit value and assert the component deploys by diffing from $DEPLOYED (fallback), not skipped or redeployed forever.
evidence: autodeploy.sh added: `mcp_deployed="$(cat "$MCP_SHA_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"` then `if [ -z "$mcp_deployed" ] || ! git -C "$MIRROR_DIR" rev-parse --verify -q "$mcp_deployed^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then mcp_deployed="$DEPLOYED"; fi`
Comment claims: 'an empty or garbage marker falls back to the global $DEPLOYED rather than poisoning the diff range.'

search_files for `rev-parse --verify`, `falls back`, and `garbage` in tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py all return (no matches) — no test seeds an empty or invalid marker file to exercise the fallback branch.
advisory.finding: The newly added marker-validation fallback (empty or unparseable mcp-deployed-sha / bot-deployed-sha resolves to $DEPLOYED via `git rev-parse --verify`) has no test. A concrete violating input — writing `not-a-sha` (or any non-commit string) into $STATE_DIR/mcp-deployed-sha — must fall back to diffing from $DEPLOYED, but no test writes a garbage marker; a regression that let the invalid value flow into `changed_range` (poisoning the diff and either skipping a real deploy or redeploying forever) would stay green.
scenarios: A box has an mcp-deployed-sha (or bot-deployed-sha) file truncated / corrupted / holding a since-gc'd sha; the tick must diff from $DEPLOYED, not from the invalid value.

evidence: Added script lines 548-551: `mcp_deployed="$(cat "$MCP_SHA_FILE" ...)"` then `if [ -z "$mcp_deployed" ] || ! git -C "$MIRROR_DIR" rev-parse --verify -q "$mcp_deployed^{commit}" ...; then mcp_deployed="$DEPLOYED"; fi`
Added script lines 552-555 apply the same guard for bot_deployed via BOT_SHA_FILE.

tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:1026 (the stub used by _mcp_box_shared_change): `rev-parse) cat "__TARGET_FILE__"; exit 0 ;;` — always succeeds, so a garbage marker such as writing 'zzzz' into mcp-deployed-sha would never drive the ! rev-parse fallback.
No new test writes an invalid/garbage sha into MCP_SHA_FILE or BOT_SHA_FILE and asserts the deploy still diffs from $DEPLOYED rather than treating the garbage marker as a valid range endpoint.
advisory.finding: The newly added marker-validation fallback (empty/unparseable component marker falls back to $DEPLOYED) is never exercised: the git stub used by every new test unconditionally returns exit 0 for `rev-parse`, so `git rev-parse --verify -q "$mcp_deployed^{commit}"` always succeeds and the fallback branch that guards against a poisoned diff range is dead in tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the shared git stub so `rev-parse --verify -q <x>^{commit}` returns non-zero for a non-target sha, then add a test writing a garbage marker and asserting the mcp/bot block still computes the delta against $DEPLOYED.

coaching.coaching: Add a regression test covering config-block re-diff noise during mcp backoff window.
coaching.subject: config-block re-diff noise during mcp backoff window

bugfix_size_gate.reason: the code the plan was reviewed against drifted: 2 dependency file(s) changed (infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh, tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py)

evidence: deploy_review_bot writes the marker but has no clear_backoff: `echo "$TARGET" > "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" "$BOT_SHA_FILE"` at autodeploy.sh:687, then `prune_docker_caches`/`log ... redeployed + healthy` and return
mcp mirror DOES clear inline: `clear_mcp_backoff` at autodeploy.sh:816 immediately after writing MCP_SHA_FILE

`clear_backoff` has exactly one call site (autodeploy.sh:886), inside the footer that is bypassed by `if [ "$bot_deferred" = 1 ] || [ "$bot_incomplete" = 1 ] || [ "$mcp_incomplete" = 1 ]; then exit 0` at autodeploy.sh:828
Concrete path: bot backoff window elapsed -> deploy_review_bot succeeds -> mcp delta pending with open window sets mcp_incomplete=1 -> exit 828 -> stale BACKOFF_FILE persists
dropped.finding: On bot success the shared bot backoff file is not cleared inline; it is cleared only at the footer (clear_backoff, line 886), which is skipped when the tick exits early at the incomplete/deferred guard (line 828) or on an mcp fatal exit. A bot that deployed successfully can therefore leave a stale deploy-backoff file (target==$TARGET, elapsed next-epoch, stale fail-count) — inconsistent with the mcp path, which deliberately clears its own backoff inline at line 816 to avoid depending on the footer.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add `clear_backoff` inside deploy_review_bot right after writing BOT_SHA_FILE (near line 687), mirroring the mcp block's inline clear_mcp_backoff at line 816.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the detect-only config_manual signal is not re-emitted on every tick while mcp is backed off / incomplete (stale $DEPLOYED), or gate it so it fires once per target.
evidence: `changed() { changed_range "$DEPLOYED" "$TARGET" "$1"; }` (line 543) — diffs the GLOBAL $DEPLOYED, which does not advance during an mcp backoff/incomplete tick
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:717-720: mcp backoff sets `mcp_incomplete=1` and the tick continues instead of the pre-fix top-level `exit 0`
Old top gate removed: `-if [ "$bo_sha" = "$TARGET" ] && [ "$(now)" -lt "${bo_next:-0}" ]; then ... exit 0` previously short-circuited before the config block on a backed-off tick
dropped.finding: While the mcp component is in a backoff window (or otherwise `*_incomplete`), the global `$DEPLOYED` never advances, so the detect-only config block re-diffs `$DEPLOYED..$TARGET` and re-emits the `config_manual` AUTODEPLOY marker/err on every ~2-minute tick for the entire mcp backoff window. Previously the top-of-script shared backoff gate `exit 0`d before reaching this block, so the config signal fired at most once per target; scoping backoff to mcp and letting the tick continue turns a one-shot operator signal into repeating alarm/log noise.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether OBS/CERTBOT re-materialization should still run on an mcp_incomplete tick (they are non-fatal and idempotent) rather than being skipped for the whole mcp backoff window.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:841: `if changed "$OBS_PATHS"; then` and :864 `if changed "$CERTBOT_PATHS"; then` sit AFTER the exit-0 guard
OBS block rationale (line 836): 'the installed copy would silently go stale (bug dying-verastile-quelea: 10 days stale)' — the failure mode this guard now re-opens for the mcp backoff window
dropped.finding: When mcp is skipped by an open backoff window with a pending delta (`mcp_incomplete=1`), the tick exits at line 828 before the host-observability and certbot re-materialization blocks and before the global deployed-sha advance. A pending OBS_PATHS or CERTBOT_PATHS change entirely unrelated to mcp is therefore deferred for the whole mcp backoff window, leaving the installed host probe/certbot units stale — the exact staleness class those blocks were added to prevent.
